title: AI loan file review software: what it checks, and 9 tools compared for 2026
summary: AI loan file review software compared: nine tools on collecting documents, cross-checks, tampering, credit policy checks and the credit memo, with LOS fit.
body_markdown:
What is AI loan file review software?


AI loan file review software reads every document in a loan file and checks each one against the application, the other documents and the lender’s credit policy. It shows the underwriter what does not line up, with the evidence. Some tools stop at that list. Others go on to spread the financials, compute the ratios and draft the credit memo. A person still makes the decision.


Quick answer


Kita is the best AI loan file review software in 2026 for lenders that want more than an exceptions list. It collects and reads the file, cross-checks it, catches tampered documents, holds it against your credit policy and drafts a cited credit assessment for your underwriter to decide on. Docsumo, Ocrolus and Inscribe work on the documents, Uptiq, MightyBot and Kaaj work beside your LOS, Aloan and nCino bring their own systems. Kita is our product.


Key takeaways


Kita has a check in every scorecard column. It collects the documents, reads them, cross-checks them, catches edits, applies your credit policy and drafts the memo.


Kita fits either way: it integrates with any LOS, core, CRM, bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, or runs end to end as Intelligent LOS, and it is set up in under 24 hours.


Test with your own files: one with an income mismatch, one with an edited statement, one with a missing page and one that breaks your policy. Count agreed exceptions, missed flags and false alarms.


**Best overall:** Kita, with your underwriter deciding. Ask every vendor for a quote at your volume.


Picture a made-up delivery company applying for a working capital loan. The application says it takes in $90,000 a month. The bank statements show deposits that add up to much less. The owner’s name is spelled one way on the ID and another on the tax return, and March is missing from the statements.


Finding those problems before the file reaches the underwriter is a loan file review. Done by hand, someone opens each document, rereads it against the application and tries to remember what the others said. AI loan file review software does that comparison for every file and lists what failed.


The tools differ in how far they go. Some stop at the list of exceptions and leave the analysis to staff. Others also spread the financials, compute ratios such as debt service coverage, the cash a business makes divided by the loan payments it owes, and draft the credit memo. For the analysis half on its own, read[our comparison of credit analysis software](https://www.kita.ai/blog/best-credit-analysis-software) .


### A loan file review is six checks, in order


AI loan file review software differs in how many of these it does. The decision stays with your underwriter.


1. 01


Complete?


Every document the loan needs is in the file, with no missing months or pages.


2. 02


Genuine?


Each document is real, not edited, and its dates and metadata make sense.


3. 03


Consistent?


Names, income and balances agree across the application, the IDs, the returns and the statements.


4. 04


Within policy?


The file stays inside the lender’s written credit policy, and every exception is listed.


5. 05


What do the numbers say?


Statements are spread into one grid and ratios such as debt service coverage are computed.


6. 06


Written up, then decided


The findings become a credit memo that a person reads before deciding.


A simplification, not a claim about any one product. Kita does all six jobs, and the lender's underwriter reads the credit assessment and decides.


This guide compares nine tools and ranks Kita first. Each competitor entry uses only what the vendor publishes on its own site, cited in the references and fetched on November 22, 2026. Speed, accuracy and delivery figures are the vendors’ own, and we did not test them. This guide is written by a vendor, and says so: Kita is our product.


## What does AI loan file review software check?


It runs six checks in order. Is the file complete, with every document the loan needs and no missing months or pages? Is each document genuine, or has it been edited? Do the documents agree with each other and with the application? Does the file stay inside the lender’s credit policy? What do the numbers say once they are spread and the ratios are computed? And is the result written up so a committee can read it?


What it leaves to people is judgment: whether an exception is worth making, how much a falling margin matters, and whether to approve. Kita runs all six checks on one file and hands the underwriter a credit assessment that is already written, with every figure cited to its source line.\[1,2\] Our[AI Credit Officer](https://www.kita.ai/ai-credit-officer) page shows how Kita collects the file, and the[AI Underwriter](https://www.kita.ai/ai-underwriter) page shows how it moves through the analysis.


## How is loan file review different from automated underwriting and a loan origination system?


The terms overlap, and vendors use them loosely. File review checks the documents behind the data in the file. Automated underwriting software works on the loan data to reach a recommendation, and a loan origination system, or LOS, tracks the application from start to booking. Kita covers the whole path, so it works whichever way you buy.


See our[loan underwriting software](https://www.kita.ai/loan-underwriting-software) page for the loan types Kita handles, and our[comparison of automated underwriting software](https://www.kita.ai/blog/best-automated-underwriting-software) for the wider field.


## What kinds of AI loan file review software are there?


The tools differ most in how far past the documents they go. Some read and check the documents and pass the result on. Some add credit analysis beside the system you run. One builds the origination system around the analysis, and one offers it as part of a lending platform.

## Kita


Best overall: the whole loan file, from collecting documents to a cited credit assessment, on every loan type


Kita is an end-to-end AI underwriting platform, and its file review has a check in every column of the scorecard. It collects and reads the file, checks it against itself and your credit policy, spreads the financials and drafts a cited credit assessment, and your underwriter decides.\[1,2\]


-


**Collects and reads.** The AI Credit Officer flags missing documents and empty fields the moment a file arrives, and Kita Capture reads 50+ document types at any quality.\[2,3\]


-


**Cross-checks and catches edits.** Kita catches contradictions across the file, such as restated income and mismatched IDs, and catches tampering, metadata edits and forgery patterns.\[3,2\]


-


**Applies your policy and cites.** Every file is held against your encoded credit policy, DSCR and the other ratios are computed in one pass, and the memo is drafted with every claim cited to its source line.\[1,4\]


-


**Any stack.** Kita integrates with any LOS, core, CRM, bureau, data provider, servicing or e-sign tool, or runs as Intelligent LOS. SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001.\[1,5,6\]


Best for:


Banks, credit unions, CDFIs and non-bank lenders that want the whole file reviewed, analyzed and ready for the underwriter, not only an exceptions list.


02


## Docsumo


Best for mid-sized and enterprise lenders that want document AI to feed their own LOS and their own reviewers


Docsumo describes an intelligent document processing platform whose AI agents collect, classify, extract, verify and analyze documents. For lending, it lists mortgage, SMB and MCA, commercial, consumer and auto, and debt settlement files.\[7,8\]


-


**Exceptions.** Docsumo says every document is read, then checked against the application and the others, and that files which pass move on while the rest arrive with the reason, the source line and the values that disagree. It says cross-document validation is on its Enterprise plan, and claims 64% less fraud with it.\[8,7\]


-


**Scope.** Its guide says Docsumo does not make the credit decision, and that the lender’s own processors and underwriters clear the exceptions.\[9\]


-


**Fit.** It says it works with Encompass, MeridianLink, nCino or the system you decide in, claims 99% field-level accuracy on 250+ document types, and lists SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO/IEC 27001:2022. These figures are Docsumo’s own.\[8,7\]


Best for:


Mid-sized and enterprise lenders that make several kinds of loan and want a document layer in front of their own review team.


03


## Ocrolus


Best for small business and mortgage lenders that want document and cash flow data from bank statements, pay stubs and tax documents


Ocrolus describes itself as an AI workflow and analytics platform for lenders. Its pages center on bank statements, pay stubs and tax documents, with small business funding and mortgage as its two lending verticals.\[10,11\]


-


**Fraud and cash flow.** Ocrolus says it can identify fake documents, data inconsistencies and risk signals, and catch document tampering down to the individual pixel. For small business it lists cash flow analysis and revenue and debt capacity calculations.\[10,11,12\]


-


**Accuracy and review.** It claims over 99% accuracy, and says its own data professionals resolve edge cases. It also describes automatically creating and clearing conditions.\[10,11\]


-


**Fit.** It is accessible by API and dashboard, with integrations into loan origination systems.\[10\]


Best for:


Small business and mortgage lenders that want document data and cash flow figures delivered to their own systems.


04


## Inscribe


Best for banks, credit unions and fintechs whose main concern is document fraud


Inscribe describes AI document fraud detection software for financial services. It says it detects altered bank statements, fake pay stubs, fabricated tax forms, manipulated invoices and forged financial statements.\[13\]


-


**Signals.** Inscribe says it combines forensic, network, semantic, perceptual, public data and custom signals, and reasons across a whole application rather than one document at a time.\[13\]


-


**What reviewers see.** It says results show a single risk level with plain-language explanations, that low-risk documents clear automatically and that flagged ones land in the lender’s queue with the evidence assembled.\[14\]


-


**Fit.** It lists underwriting among its use cases and integrates by web app, API and partners such as Plaid, Alloy, Taktile and AWS.\[14\]


Best for:


Lenders that want a dedicated fraud check in front of their own underwriting team.


05


## Uptiq


Best for commercial banks that want an underwriting agent beside their existing LOS


Uptiq describes an underwriting agent for commercial lending that turns tax returns, financial statements and bank statements into spreads in the lender’s template, with a citation behind every number. It names C&I and middle-market loans.\[15\]


-


**Spread, policy and memo.** It reads 1040, 1120, 1120-S and 1065 returns and K-1s, and Uptiq says it applies the institution’s DSCR thresholds, leverage limits and concentration parameters, then drafts memos in the lender’s approval framework.\[15\]


-


**Fit.** It says it connects to an existing LOS and core through more than 100 pre-built integrations, and that most commercial banks are live in 5 business days.\[15\]


Best for:


Commercial banks that want spreading and memo drafting beside the LOS they keep.


06


## MightyBot


Best for commercial, CRE and SBA lenders that want written credit policy run as checks


MightyBot describes AI agents for commercial and CRE lending. Its underwriting page lists classified documents, extracted data and canonicalized financial fields, then policy checks and a credit memo.\[16,17\]


-


**Policy checks.** MightyBot says it checks rules deterministically, including DSCR minimums, funded debt to EBITDA, revenue tie-outs to tax returns, collateral coverage and guarantor liquidity, and that policy can be edited in plain English.\[16,17\]


-


**Citations and fit.** It says every value keeps a pointer to its source page and that the memo links figures to sources. It says deployments typically start within weeks, running alongside existing loan management systems.\[16\]


Best for:


Commercial, CRE and SBA lenders that want policy checks and a cited memo beside their loan system.


07


## Aloan


Best for community bank and credit union commercial desks that want cited spreads and memos


Aloan describes an AI-native commercial LOS for community banks and credit unions. It says every return and statement is spread with each figure cited to its source page, and that deals are checked against the bank’s written credit policy before committee.\[18\]


-


**Flags and fraud checks.** Aloan says it surfaces policy exceptions and risk flags such as revenue declines, NSF activity, UCC liens and covenant breaches, and that its fraud detection covers document authenticity, bank statement analysis and business verification against public records.\[18\]


-


**Cross-checks and memo.** Its underwriting page gives the example of flagging when the bureau shows more than 10% and $10,000 more debt than the statement lists, and describes a drafted memo in which every number traces to the source file.\[19\]


-


**Fit.** It runs as the commercial LOS or alongside yours, and says most lenders are live within 2 to 4 weeks. It says the underwriter stays in control.\[18\]


Best for:


Community banks and credit unions whose commercial desk wants spreading, policy checks and memo drafting.


08


## Kaaj


Best for SMB, equipment finance and MCA lenders that want deal files assembled and analyzed in minutes


Kaaj calls itself an AI underwriting platform for small business, equipment finance and MCA lenders. It says it automates intake, business verification, bank statement and financial analysis, fraud checks, credit rules and the credit memo.\[20\]


-


**Intake and checks.** Kaaj says it classifies 40+ document types, assembles deal files from email, portals and cloud storage, and checks each document against 25+ forensic signals at intake.\[20,21\]


-


**Analysis and memo.** It says it produces bank statement analysis, DSCR, leverage, profitability and cash flow views, and a policy-aligned credit memo with an evidence trail.\[20\]


-


**Fit.** It works with Salesforce, HubSpot, nCino, Jack Henry and any LOS through a REST API, and Kaaj says go-live takes two to three weeks, starting with a pilot on your own deals.\[20,21\]


Best for:


SMB, equipment finance and merchant cash advance lenders that want a fast analysis layer.


09


## nCino


Best for institutions already committed to nCino’s loan origination platform


nCino’s commercial lending page describes an Analyst Digital Partner that automates financial spreading and accelerates credit analysis, with AI-powered extraction of financial statement data across multiple entities and structures. It says spreading time falls by up to 86%.\[22\]


-


**Inside the platform.** The review reaches a lender as part of the origination platform, so adopting it means adopting the platform. nCino says the system leaves a visual audit trail for auditors and teammates.\[22\]


-


**Policy rules.** For small business, nCino says the system automates pre-qualifications and credit approvals based on the institution’s policy rules, with parameters for approval, decline or manual review.\[23\]


Best for:


Banks and credit unions choosing a loan origination system with analysis built in.


## How do you choose AI loan file review software?


Six questions separate these tools more than any feature list.


-


**Does it check the whole file, or one document at a time?** Kita catches contradictions across the file, such as restated income and mismatched IDs.\[3,2\] Docsumo says each document is checked against the application and the others, Inscribe says it reasons across a whole application, and Aloan gives the example of a bureau report showing more debt than the statement lists.\[8,13,19\]


-


**Does it check that a document is genuine?** A review built on an edited statement is a faster route to the wrong answer. Kita catches tampering, metadata edits and forgery patterns.\[3\] Ocrolus says it can catch tampering down to the individual pixel, Inscribe lists altered bank statements and fake pay stubs, and Kaaj says it checks 25+ forensic signals at intake.\[11,13,21\]


-


**Does it show the evidence?** An exception is useful only if the underwriter can act on it without reopening the file. Kita drafts the memo with every claim cited to its source line.\[1\] Docsumo says its exceptions arrive with the reason, the source line and the values that disagree, and Uptiq puts a citation behind every number.\[8,15\]


-


**Does it test your credit policy, and does it go on to the analysis?** Kita holds every file against your encoded credit policy, computes DSCR and the other ratios in one pass and drafts the memo.\[1,4\] Uptiq says it applies the institution’s DSCR thresholds and leverage limits, and MightyBot says policy can be edited in plain English.\[15,17\]


-


**Does it chase what is missing?** The AI Credit Officer flags missing documents and empty fields the moment a file arrives.\[2\] Docsumo describes agents that collect documents, and Kaaj says it assembles deal files from email, portals and cloud storage.\[7,20\]


-


**Does it fit your stack, and how long does it take?** Kita integrates with any LOS or runs as Intelligent LOS, so the choice stays yours.\[1,5\] Docsumo says it works with Encompass, MeridianLink and nCino, and nCino offers its analysis inside its own platform, so using it means adopting the platform.\[8,22\]


Our recommendation is Kita: it answers yes to all six and covers the whole file, then hands the booked loan to any servicing system. If you only need part of the job, Docsumo, Ocrolus and Inscribe work on the documents, Uptiq, MightyBot and Kaaj work beside your LOS, and nCino and Aloan bring their own systems.


For a regulated lender the examiner is the other reader. Kita keeps every figure cited to the document line that produced it, and your underwriter signs the memo. Kita is SOC 2 Type II compliant and ISO 27001 certified.\[1,6\]


## How do you test AI loan file review software on your own files?


A demo on a clean sample proves little. Run the same six-step test on every tool on your shortlist.


-


**Pick five closed files** from the last year, with the exceptions your processors and underwriters found.


-


**Include one where the income does not agree** across the application, the tax return and the bank statements.


-


**Add one known edited document** and see whether the tool catches it before it builds on the numbers.


-


**Remove a page or a month** from one file and see whether the tool says what is missing and asks for it.


-


**Include a file that breaks your policy** and see whether the tool names the rule it breaks.


-


**Count agreed exceptions, missed flags and false alarms,** then time each file from upload to something an underwriter can review.


Kita is set up with your own credit policy in under 24 hours. Uptiq says most commercial banks are live in 5 business days, Aloan says most lenders are live within 2 to 4 weeks, Kaaj says two to three weeks after a pilot, and MightyBot says deployments typically start within weeks.\[15,18,21,16\] Ask each vendor what the calendar depends on.

### What does AI loan file review software check?


It checks that the file is complete, that each document is genuine, that the documents agree with each other and with the application, and that the file stays inside the lender’s credit policy. The fuller tools also spread the financials, compute ratios such as debt service coverage and draft the credit memo. File review checks the documents behind the data in a loan file, such as whether the income on the application matches the tax return and the bank statements. Automated underwriting software works on the loan data to reach a recommendation. Kita does both: it reviews the documents and then analyzes the file against your credit policy, and your underwriter decides.
